summary: Guitar Hero entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Guitar Hero
entries.definitive_edition: Original PlayStation 2 release with guitar controller

emulation.emulator: PCSX2 only if original hardware is unavailable
emulation.notes: If emulating, use a reliable guitar-controller adapter and document latency calibration carefully.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS2 hardware with intended guitar controller

primary.version: Original PS2 release with guitar controller
primary.why: The first Guitar Hero is a PS2-era rhythm game built around its guitar controller. Original hardware or a low-latency PS2 setup preserves the peripheral and timing experience better than treating it like a generic controller game.
primary.how_to_play: Use a PS2 copy with the original guitar controller, calibrate display latency, and record controller model, display type, difficulty, and any unlock/bonus-song state.

all_releases.reason: primary: only original release platform and the intended controller experience.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The main issue is latency/peripheral preservation rather than a competing definitive edition.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced modern remaster route replaces the original PS2 release.

entries.title: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock
entries.definitive_edition: No modern definitive edition; PC retail for base-game capture, with preserved console DLC documented separately

emulation.emulator: Not required for PC; Dolphin/Xenia/RPCS3 only for console comparison
emulation.notes: Use original PC retail or original console hardware when controller latency matters.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC retail at high resolution for base game; original console hardware for preserved DLC/peripheral state

primary.version: PC retail release with compatible guitar controller
primary.why: For the base game, the PC release is the cleanest high-resolution capture route. The archive still needs to document controller hardware, unavailable/delisted online or DLC context, and console-specific issues such as the original Wii mono-audio disc problem.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PC retail build with a compatible USB guitar controller. Record patch state, controller model/adapter, calibration, resolution, audio latency, setlist/DLC availability, and whether console DLC or online features were compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only if preserving already-owned DLC or documenting online history.
secondary.why: PC is better for base-game capture, but console DLC history can affect completeness if preserved.

secondary.what_to_play: Use the corrected disc only if documenting Wii-specific behavior.
secondary.why: The original Wii release had a documented mono-audio issue.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release family with instrument controllers and console ecosystem differences.
all_releases.reason: secondary: use for DLC, online, controller, or Wii-audio documentation.

all_releases.fidelity: High-resolution PC/Mac route for the base game, with controller and compatibility caveats.

all_releases.reason: secondary: document only if content is already owned/preserved and playable.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC is the best base-game capture route, but console DLC/online history and Wii audio corrections should be documented separately when relevant.

entries.remaster_caveats: Requires compatible guitar/controller hardware and calibration. Record DLC/online availability because old services and downloads are not guaranteed.

entries.title: Guitar Hero World Tour
entries.definitive_edition: PC retail for base game; GHWT: Definitive Edition only as a labeled modded route

emulation.emulator: None for PC; Dolphin/Xenia/RPCS3/PCSX2 only for console comparison
emulation.notes: Use original instruments or reliable adapters and record calibration.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC retail at high resolution for base game; original console hardware for preserved DLC/peripheral state

primary.version: PC retail release, with GHWT: Definitive Edition only if documented as a modded route
primary.why: World Tour shipped across console and PC platforms with full-band instruments and a music-studio feature. For base-game capture, PC provides the highest-resolution route, but controller/drum/mic compatibility and old DLC/service state require careful documentation; community GHWT: Definitive Edition can be useful but should be labeled as a mod route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PC retail build with compatible guitar/drum/mic hardware and latency calibration. Record patch, controller/adapters, calibration, instrument mix, setlist/DLC availability, Music Studio/GHTunes state, resolution, and whether GHWT:DE or console DLC was included.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original console instrument and DLC/service ecosystems
secondary.what_to_play: Use only for preserved DLC, online/GHTunes history, or peripheral comparison.
secondary.why: PC is better for base-game capture, but console service history can matter for completeness.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only as a labeled modded route.
secondary.why: It changes the base route and may add content beyond the original release.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console full-band routes with platform-specific instruments and services.
High-resolution desktop route for the base game, with controller and compatibility caveats.
all_releases.reason: primary: best base-game capture route if hardware works.

all_releases.fidelity: Community-maintained mod route with expanded compatibility/content expectations.
all_releases.reason: secondary: labeled mod route, not a silent replacement for the retail game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC has the base-game capture ceiling, while console DLC/peripheral ecosystems and GHWT:DE mod content can affect completeness if preserved.

entries.remaster_caveats: Old DLC/GHTunes/service content may be unavailable. Controller and audio latency must be documented.

entries.title: Guitar Hero II
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360 disc route with compatible guitar controller and owned DLC documented

emulation.notes: Use original console/guitar hardware; emulation is not the baseline for rhythm timing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox 360 hardware with calibrated guitar controller

primary.version: Guitar Hero II Xbox 360 disc, with owned DLC documented if available
primary.why: The PlayStation 2 version is the original release, but the Xbox 360 version adds HD output, extra on-disc songs, and a now-historical DLC path. For a complete capture route, use Xbox 360 with guitar controller and document DLC entitlement; use PS2 for original-launch comparison.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Xbox 360 disc with a compatible guitar controller. Record console, display lag calibration, controller model, difficulty, career/co-op state, bonus songs, on-disc extras, DLC entitlement if already owned, and whether PS2 original was compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original launch route and PS2 guitar context
secondary.why: Xbox 360 has the broader HD/extra-song route, while PS2 is the launch artifact.

all_releases.fidelity: Original launch release with PS2 guitar controller.
HD console release with extra songs and DLC entitlement path.
all_releases.reason: primary: broadest official content/capture route if DLC is owned.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PS2 is the original, while Xbox 360 has HD output, extra songs, and historical DLC entitlement caveats.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record controller, calibration, and DLC entitlement; do not substitute later Guitar Hero setlists.
